title: Sell Mineral Rights in Montgomery, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Montgomery, PA | Lycoming County
metaDescription: Montgomery, PA along the West Branch Susquehanna in Lycoming County. We buy dry-gas Marcellus mineral rights directly, with a plain title and royalty review.
heroLead: Montgomery sits on the West Branch of the Susquehanna in Lycoming County, farm country that turned out to hold some of the more consistently productive dry-gas Marcellus rock in the northeast part of the state.
intro: Lycoming County's river-bottom farms have been in some families for generations, and when Marcellus leasing arrived in this part of the state, a lot of that farmland got pooled into large horizontal units almost overnight. If you're holding a fractional interest from land near Montgomery, it's likely tied to one of those larger units even if your family's original tract was modest in size.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Montgomery directly. We look at your deed, your lease, and your royalty history, and explain each piece before making an offer.

sections.heading: West Branch Farmland in the Dry-Gas Core
paragraphs: The Susquehanna's West Branch cuts through some of the better dry-gas Marcellus territory in Lycoming County, and operators have developed multi-well pads throughout the townships surrounding Montgomery over the past decade plus. Production here is straight methane without the liquids complications that show up farther southwest.

That doesn't mean royalty checks are simple, though. Gathering and compression deductions still apply, and understanding your lease's specific language on those costs matters as much here as anywhere else.

sections.heading: Tracing Family Farm Title
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Lycoming County Recorder of Deeds in Williamsport, which often means working through farm-boundary descriptions that predate modern surveying in this part of the county.
If your interest was inherited rather than leased directly by you, we'll help confirm exactly how it passed down and whether the paperwork is clean enough for a straightforward transfer.

sections.heading: What We'll Explain Before Any Offer
paragraphs: We'll go through your division order and royalty statements with you so the decimal interest, allocated production, and deductions all make sense before a number ever comes up.

faqs.question: Is my river-bottom farmland treated differently for leasing purposes?
faqs.answer: Not in terms of mineral value, though older farm-boundary descriptions in this area sometimes take extra care to reconcile with modern unit maps during title research.

faqs.question: My family's land near Montgomery was pooled into a large unit. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Horizontal units in Lycoming County frequently combine many smaller legacy farm tracts, so being part of a larger pooled unit is common rather than unusual.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests that haven't produced in a while?
faqs.answer: We evaluate those individually based on the well's history and nearby activity, and we'll give you an honest assessment either way.
